Markov Stability Analysis

Mohammed Saqr

University of Eastern Finland

Sonsoles López-Pernas

University of Eastern Finland

Kamila Misiejuk

FernUniversität in Hagen, Germany
Source: vignettes/markov-stability.Rmd
markov-stability.Rmd

In a complex-systems view of learning, a state is stable when students who reach it tend to remain in it and students who leave it tend to return (Saqr, Dever, et al. 2025; Saqr, López-Pernas & Tikka 2026). López-Pernas and Saqr (2024) described student engagement in these terms, as the momentum of achievement and the inertia of disengagement. Markov chain theory measures stability from a transition network (Kemeny & Snell 1976). For a first-order chain with transition matrix PP and stationary distribution π\pi:

  • the persistence of state ii is PiiP_{ii}, the probability of remaining in it at the next step;
  • the sojourn time is 1/(1−Pii)1 / (1 - P_{ii}), the expected number of consecutive steps spent in it once entered;
  • the stationary probability πi\pi_i is the long-run share of steps spent in it, and the return time 1/πi1 / \pi_i is the expected number of steps between two visits;
  • the mean first passage time mijm_{ij} is the expected number of steps to reach state jj for the first time from state ii.

In Nestimate (Saqr, López-Pernas & Misiejuk 2026), passage_time() returns the matrix of mean first passage times and markov_stability() the per-state measures. Both accept a network, a transition matrix, or a group of networks.

Data

trajectories records the engagement state of 138 students in each of the 15 successive courses of a program. The states are the three engagement states of Saqr and López-Pernas (2021): Active, Average and Disengaged. Saqr and López-Pernas (2021) and Saqr, López-Pernas, Jovanović and Gašević (2023) followed such engagement trajectories across the courses of a full program. The data have one row per student and one column per course; a missing value occurs only as a run at the end of a row and marks the point at which a student left the program.

The transition network

build_network() estimates the probability of moving from each state to each state between consecutive courses.

library(Nestimate)
net <- build_network(trajectories, method = "relative")
net
#> Transition Network (relative probabilities) [directed]
#>   Weights: [0.035, 0.698]  |  mean: 0.333
#> 
#>   Strongest edges (9 of 9):
#>    from       to         weight
#>    Active     Active     0.698 
#>    Average    Average    0.610 
#>    Disengaged Disengaged 0.483 
#>    Disengaged Average    0.397 
#>    Active     Average    0.267 
#>    Average    Active     0.204 
#>    Average    Disengaged 0.186 
#>    Disengaged Active     0.120 
#>    Active     Disengaged 0.035  
#> 
#>   extract_edges(include_self = TRUE) lists every edge; extract_transition_matrix() gives the weight matrix;
#>   extract_initial_probs() the initial probabilities.

The probabilities leaving each state sum to 1. A student who is Active in one course is Active in the next with probability 0.698, Average with probability 0.267 and Disengaged with probability 0.035. The measures below are computed from this matrix, so they assume that the transition probabilities are the same in every course and that the next state depends only on the current one.

Mean first passage times 

pt <- passage_time(net)
print(pt, digits = 2)
#> Mean First Passage Times (3 states)
#> 
#>            Active Average Disengaged
#> Active       2.69    3.63      10.36
#> Average      5.51    2.26       7.97
#> Disengaged   6.16    2.78       5.41
#> 
#> Stationary distribution:
#>     Active    Average Disengaged 
#>     0.3719     0.4431     0.1850
plot(pt)

Row ii, column jj of the matrix is the expected number of courses for a student in state ii to reach state jj for the first time; the diagonal is the return time. A student in Active takes 3.6 courses on average to reach Average and 10.4 courses to reach Disengaged. In the reverse direction, a student in Disengaged takes 6.2 courses to reach Active and 2.8 courses to reach Average. Decline from Active to Disengaged is therefore slower than recovery in the opposite direction, and both pass mostly through Average. The values are expectations under the fitted chain; a value longer than the 15 courses of the program describes the chain, not a time that was observed.

Stability of the states 

ms <- markov_stability(net)
summary(ms)
#>        state persistence stationary_prob return_time sojourn_time
#> 1     Active      0.6976          0.3719        2.69         3.31
#> 2    Average      0.6099          0.4431        2.26         2.56
#> 3 Disengaged      0.4831          0.1850        5.41         1.93
#>   avg_time_to_others avg_time_from_others
#> 1               6.99                 5.84
#> 2               6.74                 3.20
#> 3               4.47                 9.16
plot(ms)

persistence, stationary_prob, return_time and sojourn_time are the measures defined above. avg_time_to_others is the mean passage time from the state to the other states, and avg_time_from_others the mean passage time from the other states to it; a state with a short avg_time_from_others is reached quickly from anywhere.

Active is the most persistent state: its persistence is 0.698 and its sojourn time 3.31 courses. Average is the most accessible: it is reached from the other states in 3.20 courses on average, and it has the largest stationary probability, 0.443. Disengaged is the least persistent (0.483, a sojourn of 1.93 courses) and the least accessible (9.16 courses), and it is the state students spend the least time in (0.185).

Groups of students

A single chain for all students averages over students whose engagement develops differently. Sequence clustering groups the students by the similarity of their sequences (Saqr, López-Pernas, Helske, et al. 2024), and a transition network can then be estimated for each group (López-Pernas, Tikka & Saqr 2025). build_clusters() computes the Hamming distance between sequences, the number of courses in which two students are in different states (Hamming 1950), and partitions the students around medoids (Kaufman & Rousseeuw 1990). Three clusters are used here as a working choice.

clusters <- build_clusters(trajectories, k = 3, seed = 2026)
clusters
#> Sequence Clustering [pam]
#>   Sequences: 138  |  Clusters: 3
#>   Dissimilarity: hamming
#>   Quality: silhouette = 0.360
#> 
#>   Cluster  N           Mean within-dist  Medoid
#>   1        47 (34.1%)  5.898             124
#>   2        74 (53.6%)  8.389             44
#>   3        17 (12.3%)  5.412             103

The three clusters have 47, 74 and 17 students. The average silhouette is 0.36 (Rousseeuw 1987), a moderate separation. build_network() on the clustering estimates one transition network per cluster, and state_distribution() shows the states that make up each cluster.

cluster_networks <- build_network(clusters)
state_distribution(cluster_networks)
#>       group      state count proportion
#> 1 Cluster 1     Active   528 0.75213675
#> 2 Cluster 1    Average   139 0.19800570
#> 3 Cluster 1 Disengaged    35 0.04985755
#> 4 Cluster 2    Average   663 0.60382514
#> 5 Cluster 2 Disengaged   263 0.23952641
#> 6 Cluster 2     Active   172 0.15664845
#> 7 Cluster 3 Disengaged    56 0.80000000
#> 8 Cluster 3    Average    11 0.15714286
#> 9 Cluster 3     Active     3 0.04285714

Cluster 1 is mostly Active (75% of its observed courses), cluster 2 mostly Average (60%), and cluster 3 mostly Disengaged (80%).

passage_time() and markov_stability() accept the group of networks and compute the measures for each cluster. summary() returns one table with a row for each cluster and state.

cluster_pt <- passage_time(cluster_networks)
summary(cluster_pt)
#>       group      state return_time stationary mean_out mean_in
#> 1 Cluster 1     Active        1.33     0.7508    16.04    1.82
#> 2 Cluster 1    Average        5.14     0.1947    13.11    5.77
#> 3 Cluster 1 Disengaged       18.36     0.0545     3.79   25.35
#> 4 Cluster 2     Active        6.60     0.1516     4.21    8.94
#> 5 Cluster 2    Average        1.63     0.6137     7.16    1.89
#> 6 Cluster 2 Disengaged        4.26     0.2347     5.57    6.11
#> 7 Cluster 3     Active       23.00     0.0435     6.50   39.50
#> 8 Cluster 3    Average        5.75     0.1739    18.75   10.00
#> 9 Cluster 3 Disengaged        1.28     0.7826    26.50    2.25
plot(cluster_pt)

cluster_ms <- markov_stability(cluster_networks)
summary(cluster_ms)
#>       group      state persistence stationary_prob return_time sojourn_time
#> 1 Cluster 1     Active      0.8048          0.7508        1.33         5.12
#> 2 Cluster 1    Average      0.2984          0.1947        5.14         1.43
#> 3 Cluster 1 Disengaged      0.3235          0.0545       18.36         1.48
#> 4 Cluster 2     Active      0.3648          0.1516        6.60         1.57
#> 5 Cluster 2    Average      0.6737          0.6137        1.63         3.06
#> 6 Cluster 2 Disengaged      0.4309          0.2347        4.26         1.76
#> 7 Cluster 3     Active      0.5000          0.0435       23.00         2.00
#> 8 Cluster 3    Average      0.5000          0.1739        5.75         2.00
#> 9 Cluster 3 Disengaged      0.8889          0.7826        1.28         9.00
#>   avg_time_to_others avg_time_from_others
#> 1              16.04                 1.82
#> 2              13.11                 5.77
#> 3               3.79                25.35
#> 4               4.21                 8.94
#> 5               7.16                 1.89
#> 6               5.57                 6.11
#> 7               6.50                39.50
#> 8              18.75                10.00
#> 9              26.50                 2.25
plot(cluster_ms)

In cluster 1, Active has persistence 0.805 and a sojourn time of 5.12 courses, and it is reached from the other states in 1.82 courses on average. Disengaged is reached from the other states in 25.35 courses on average, longer than the program: under this cluster’s chain, students rarely reach it. In cluster 2, Average is the most persistent state (0.674, a sojourn of 3.06 courses) and the most accessible (1.89 courses), and Active takes 8.94 courses to reach. In cluster 3, Disengaged has persistence 0.889 and a sojourn time of 9.00 courses.

The estimates of cluster 3 rest on few observations. Its 17 students contribute 2 transitions out of Active and 8 out of Average, so the persistence of those two states (0.500 each) and the long passage times to Active (39.50 courses from the other states) are not reliable. The number of transitions out of each state can be checked with build_network(clusters, method = "frequency") before the measures are interpreted.
